title: A 600 lines per mm grating: angle of each order
caption: With d = 1/600 mm = 1.67 μm, d sin θ = nλ puts the first-order sodium line (589 nm) at 20.7° and the second order at 45.0°. Orders exist only while nλ < d: at 700 nm just two orders appear, and a third (shown for λ < 556 nm) needs a shorter wavelength. Higher orders spread colours more.
alt: Graph of diffraction angle against wavelength from 400 to 700 nanometres for orders 1, 2 and 3 of a 600 lines per mm grating: order 1 rises to 25 degrees, order 2 rises more steeply, and order 3 exists only for wavelengths below 555 nanometres.
description: The horizontal axis is wavelength in nanometres; the vertical axis is the angle of the diffraction maximum in degrees.
Each curve is θ = sin⁻¹(nλ/d) with d = 1.67 μm for n = 1, 2, 3.
At 589 nm: first order 20.7°, second order 45.0°.
The third order ends at 556 nm, where sin θ reaches 1; at 700 nm only two orders fit (n < d/λ = 2.4).
